disagreements.point: The input inflation was never converted into points of revenue, and no price-increase percentage was derived. Beans were 10.5% of revenue, so +40% adds about 4.2 points; other inputs were 31.5%, so +37.5% adds about 11.8 points.
quotes: That 38% is the hole I'd size the pricing action against — the 16 points on the P&L is only what survived after 15% revenue growth absorbed part of it, so their true exposure is larger than the headline.
disagreements.opus_reason: Q1: the candidate treated the 38% COGS-base inflation as the hole to size pricing against, without converting it into points of revenue through COGS's share of revenue.

disagreements.point: Once pressed, you tied the specific survey numbers to the 20% share assumption and found that doctors like the product but access and presence are the binding constraints. However, the first read was a one-line assertion with no numbers, and you never noted that answers sum to more than 100% or that out-of-pocket cost (15%) is well behind coverage as a barrier.
quotes: Convenience sells it; access and lack of US presence are the binding constraints — which supports the partner route.
64% cite once-daily oral versus 58% citing coverage and 41% no local support.
so 20% is plausible with the right partner and at risk without one.
disagreements.opus_reason: The complaints are an initial read with no numbers and parts of the exhibit never noted: the over-100% sum and out-of-pocket cost against coverage. No wrong figure was stated, and the assertion itself is supported by the data. N2: an exhibit not read in full gets no tag.

disagreements.point: On the survey, the candidate correctly isolated access and local support as the two dominant barriers, but the read was a single sentence that never answered whether 20% share is defensible. It missed the 27% 'want more US experience' signal of a slow ramp and did not note that out-of-pocket cost (15%) is a minor barrier.
quotes: which supports the partnering recommendation rather than the 20% itself

Convenience pull is real, but the top two barriers — access at 58% and no local support at 41% — are both fixable by a US partner, which supports the partnering recommendation rather than the 20% itself; I'd use it to pressure-test share in diligence.
disagreements.opus_reason: The question was whether a 20% share is defensible, but the candidate tied the survey to the partnering recommendation instead. X3: an implication off the client's question.

disagreements.point: On the cohort exhibit, the candidate separated upgrades from cancellations and saw that the upgrade stream is the key value driver, but never used the Cancelled row (5% in month 1, steady) to derive Starter churn, even after the interviewer stressed that cancellation rates are steady.
quotes: Starter LTV stays $405.
Starter loses 40% to cancellation in year one, but another 20% upgrades to Pro, so only 40% are still paying $40.
disagreements.opus_reason: The interviewer stressed that cancellation rates are steady, yet the candidate kept the flawed churn method and held 'Starter LTV stays $405'. L1: hint not applied.

disagreements.point: Several claims assumed Starter churn at $60 matches churn at $40, even though the case said churn at $60 can't yet be measured.
quotes: Even at zero upgrades, $60 clears the board's rule, and shutting it down forfeits 850 incremental customers a month in a segment Pro's $1,200 sales motion can't profitably reach.
disagreements.opus_reason: The candidate assumed $60 churn equals $40 churn, which the case says can't yet be measured. That unconfirmed assumption is used as a reason supporting keeping the $60 tier. H4 defers to R2 when the claim backs the recommendation.

disagreements.point: The upside from sourcing, waste and mix was asserted but not quantified.
quotes: sourcing plus waste control and a mix shift toward food should push it higher.
disagreements.opus_reason: The upside was never quantified and no wrong number was stated. Under N2, an analysis left undone with no stated number gets no tag.

disagreements.point: Slightly understated the beans figure in the final synthesis, calling it 'about 4 points' when his own derivation gave 4.2 — minor, but rounded down in the headline.
quotes: beans alone up 40%, worth about 4 points
disagreements.opus_reason: N4: rounding 4.2 to 'about 4' is only an imprecise label, not a wrong figure, so no tag fits.

disagreements.point: No signposting or enumeration ('first... second...'); the interviewer had to repeatedly prompt for more.
quotes: Profit is a function of revenue and cost.
disagreements.opus_reason: Missing signposting gets no tag under N5. The point also says the interviewer had to keep prompting for more, which L4 tags as waiting for the interviewer.

disagreements.point: The candidate was answer-first and hypothesis-led, often stating expectations before seeing data. At the opening, though, the candidate gave conclusions before laying out any structure.
quotes: The structure is basically implied by that: revenue levers, cost levers, and the fare is the one that moves.
let me say upfront what I expect it to show, so we can test me.
disagreements.opus_reason: Under S2, giving conclusions at the opening before laying out any structure means the candidate skipped structuring and went straight to an answer.

disagreements.point: Ignored more than ten escalating hints, including Level 1 ('Take your time') and Level 2 ('Let's simplify') assists, and never incorporated any of them.
quotes: I'm not sure. Sorry.
I'm stuck, sorry. Not without a more detailed COGS breakdown.
disagreements.opus_reason: L1: the candidate received more than ten escalating hints and never applied them, which is feedback not applied after valid hints.

disagreements.point: Early on, the candidate drove the case by naming the data needed next, but that leadership faded: the candidate tried to end the case, and the brainstorm needed repeated prompting for range.
quotes: I'm done — can we do another case?
Sampling in-store to beat the taste objection, and a multi-pack or repeat-purchase coupon to drive the second buy.
My recommendation would hinge on whether that intent math clears 2 million households.
disagreements.opus_reason: Trying to end the case is conduct, so no tag (N4). The next mistake is a brainstorm lacking range, with ideas all from one area (promotion). Prompting doesn't change the tag (G4), so C1 applies: ideas all from one area.

disagreements.point: The candidate acknowledged each challenge specifically and explained the source of the error and the correction without defensiveness, but the corrections did not stick: after the funnel-base correction in turn 6, the same base-substitution error recurred with share (turn 9), the survey (turn 13) and B's share (turn 17).
quotes: I'll use the 20% share here as well — that's Aldermoor's own forecast for the product
It isn't right — the exhibit says plainly "20% of eligible patients," and I substituted the treated pool because I was thinking of share-of-therapy the way it's usually quoted in market share terms.
Fair — I quoted B's market-level sales, not what Aldermoor keeps.
disagreements.opus_reason: The candidate acknowledged the base correction but the same error recurred in later turns. L1: feedback acknowledged but not applied.

disagreements.point: After the interviewer flagged 'That's a long list of data' and asked for structure first, you kept sending long unprioritized data lists in every later turn instead of adjusting.
quotes: To populate that, could I get: one, COGS as a percent of revenue by year.
Could I get: one, the dollar revenue base.
disagreements.opus_reason: L1: acknowledged the feedback about long data lists but didn't apply it, and kept sending them.

disagreements.point: Size every lever against the gap before ruling one in or out. Two years of flat prices against roughly 38% input inflation makes pricing an obvious lever. A 10% price increase alone moves margin from about 6% to about 14.5%, while closing 16 points through cost alone would require cutting input cost per revenue dollar by about 28%. Run that comparison out loud before committing to a recommendation.
disagreements.opus_reason: J1: the candidate ruled out pricing despite flat prices against roughly 38% input inflation, a decisive fact.

disagreements.point: Reconcile the pricing magnitude: the ~38% figure restores margin on its own, so size the required price increase net of procurement gains and elasticity rather than stacking a phased 15%+15% that neither sums to 38% nor accounts for the COGS clawback.
disagreements.opus_reason: G5: the first fix is to reconcile the size of the recommended price increase. The phased 15%+15% doesn't match the analysis. R2: an impact or size that is wrong or not derived.

disagreements.point: Don't build your lead argument on an untested reading of the client's criterion. The $300M bar is Kelvexa's US net sales, which Option B also clears at $400M. Lead instead with the economics you derived correctly: building earns $240M versus $120M and stays ahead unless share falls below 12.5%. When the interviewer probes a definition, explicitly revise rather than restate.
disagreements.opus_reason: G5: the first fix is not to lead the recommendation with an untested, wrong reading of the $300M criterion. R2: a weak or unconfirmed supporting reason for the recommendation.
